newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to decide on Dutch pork imports next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to decide on Dutch pork imports next week.

text.p: The Agriculture Department will make a decision next week on what action it should take on pork imports from the Netherlands as a result of the cases of swine fever detected this week in that country, a USDA official said Friday.
Swine fever has been discovered on four farms in the Netherlands, including two new cases confirmed by the Dutch Agriculture Ministry on Friday.
A spokesman for USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said the USDA was aware of the two new cases detected, and said the department is assessing the situation.
The USDA official said the agency is watching to see if the Dutch government is taking adequate measures to "successfully control the situation."

The official also noted that there are no live hogs being imported from the Netherlands. He said USDA is determining the nature of the pork products coming into this country to assess any risk of the disease.
Poland has banned the import of pigs from the Netherlands, and Belgium has tightened its import regulations.
USDA trade adviser Paul Drazek said, "We will take the appropriate steps if need be." Drazek said that action would not necessarily mean a shut off of all imports.
The United States normally imports at least 600 million pounds of pork a year.
Over 400 million pounds of pork are imported from Canada, followed by around 150 million pounds from Denmark.
Around 10 million pounds of pork products are normally purchased from the Netherlands.
